flows.representativeInput: Temporary Git repo from tests/runtime-archive-merge-amendment.test.ts: brief accepted on a feature branch, amended once; historicalRequirement called with no record, an empty record, then a matching record. Diff c519b3f..HEAD of archive.mjs and the test read.

observations.actual: [AC:spec-5-1] passed (3 tests, exit 0). The test builds a feature branch whose brief is accepted then amended once, and asserts: with no record, historicalRequirement throws 'no docs/features/f/brief-amendments.json records its amendments; add one entry for each later brief commit, with the answered owner decision that authorized it, as .joycraft/references/archive.md shows for brief-amendments.json: <commit> (fromSha256 <hash v1>, toSha256 <hash v2>)', matching the spec's text; with an empty record it throws 'commit <commit> has no single amendment record; add one entry ... : <same entry>'; a record with those hashes and answered decision D1 then returns the amendment. Source read (payload/.joycraft/runtime/archive.mjs briefAmendments, diff c519b3f..HEAD): entryFor hashes committedBytes at commit^ and commit, the same bytes the later match check uses, so the printed hashes are the ones the record must carry; the list is joined with '; ' one item per later commit after merges that keep a parent's brief are filtered; the existing refusal paths (malformed record, hash mismatch, decision unanswered) are unchanged. The refusal itself is kept, as the brief's amendment-message section and the spec require; the existing merge-changes-brief test still matches its prefix and passes. Brief intent: keeping the refusal is right. A brief edit after acceptance changes what was reviewed; the refusal now tells the agent exactly what to record and cites archive.md, whose brief-amendments.json example has the same fields (commit, fromSha256, toSha256, decisions, summary), and it still demands an answered owner decision, so it cannot be cleared without the owner.

limits: Focused test only; project gate not rerun (implementer receipt docs/features/2026-11-22-fixes-1-9-3/receipts/spec-4-5-implementer-gate.log).

findings.summary: Spec 5 and the brief amendment-message section did not exist at the base c519b3f; both were committed in 37c0fc6, after the code commit 4a9a049. Startup therefore lists tests/runtime-archive-merge-amendment.test.ts as undeclared and its class-1 line as addedAfterBase. The change only adds one test, and the acceptance bullet requires it, so it does not block. The fails-before receipt (receipts/spec-5-implementer-fails-before.log) records revision 443cb58 dirty, a commit after the fix, so it does not show which tree failed. Other undeclared files (runtime-dispatch-commands, runtime-evidence-receipt, text-worker-commands) belong to spec 4 and earlier specs in the range.

When the brief does not exist at commit^ (deleted then re-added), entryFor prints the hash of an empty buffer as fromSha256; a record that copies it is then refused as not matching. Rare; the spec does not decide it.
The test covers one later commit only; the "one item per later commit" joining with "; " is read in source, not exercised by a two-commit fixture.

This feature's own brief changed in 37c0fc6 after specs 1 and 2 were accepted, and its frontmatter has decisions: []. If archive needs brief history for this feature, the new refusal will ask for a brief-amendments.json entry with an answered owner decision that the brief does not record yet. Check at archive time; the added sections may sit outside specs 1 and 2 scoped anchors.
